prerequisites: No prerequisites. Competencies from the modules Introduction to Cryptography and its Applications or IT-Security are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: The students can explain advanced basic principles and more complex methods of cryptography that are necessary for evaluating cryptographic security and their application in the field of IT security.
The students can explain design and analysis principles for cryptographic procedures.
The students can report on current research questions in the field of cryptography.

syllabus_topics: Deepening of essential concepts and methods of cryptography, in particular encryption, authentication, design and analysis of symmetric algorithms, elliptic curves, post-quantum cryptography, cryptographic protocols.
Introduction to current research topics in the field of cryptography.
assessment_rules: To acquire credits, at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments must be achieved. The grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
bibliography: Lars R. Knudsen, Matthew Robshaw: The Block Cipher Companion. Information Security and Cryptography, Springer 2011
Joan Daemen, Vincent Rijmen: The Design of Rijndael - The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Second Edition. Information Security and Cryptography, Springer 2020
Jonathan Katz, Yehuda Lindell: Introduction to Modern Cryptography, Second Edition. CRC Press 2014
